text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some manufacturing companies have slashed prices of their products in the hope that Christmas sales volumes will increase in the face of dwindling buying power.

- Shell's Nigerian producing unit says that state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) still owes a total of 18.97 billion naira. A company spokesman said exploration is being affected as are community programmes.

- Talks have begun between an unknown U.S. company and a Nigerian firm on the possible floation of a capital issue of $100 million on the stock exchange. The issue, expected to involve real estate developers, would also be quoted on an American exchange. The director-general of the Nigerian stock exchange said he was hopeful the deal will go through.

- A Lagos court has temporarily prohibited all parties in a dispute over who will insure NNPC in 1997 from undertaking the insurance next year. The National Insurance Company of Nigeria (NICON) is asking the court to restrain the oil minister and NNPC from paying a premium to any company other than NICON.
- Police orders heightened security nationwide following two bomb blasts which rocked Lagos this week.
- Telephone lines in the Ikeja business district of Lagos are gradually being restored at the exchange destroyed by fire several months ago.
- Nigerian Breweries foray into the soft drink market may begin on Friday as the Schweppes range of drinks acquired from Nigerian Bottling Company hits the market.
